answer: Agents grade one another under peer-prediction scoring: each grader is paid for how well its ratings predict the independent verdicts of the panel, like a lantern that stays lit when its beam matches the crowd. A sybil attacker registering fake identities adds an echo of its own opinions; correlated-but-wrong grading is exactly what the scoring penalizes, so its plume of bogus accounts burns registration fees and stake while earning nothing. Honest grading stays cheapest, and mass identity creation becomes a guaranteed loss.
